title: Service degradation hypothesis and drilldown playbook for inference
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook for investigating service degradation in our inference stacks (hosted + dedicated). Focus is on: quick hypothesis generation, high-ROI signals to check first, and a standard set of dashboards/queries for tier-1 triage.

Intended audience:
- Oncall SRE / Eng responder
- Serving runtime engineers
- Observability owners who will evolve metrics/tracing definitions

High-level approach (30/60/120s):
- 0–30s: determine blast radius and severity
  - Which tenants/routes/models are affected? Check per-route request rate and error rate rollups.
  - Is this single-region or global? Look at region tag on ingress metrics.
- 30–60s: basic hypothesis triage (isolate network / infra / model / client issue)
  - Check infra: node GPU/CPU/mem saturation, host-level OOMs, pod restarts.
  - Check runtime: token latency spike, KV cache hit rate drop, batching lag increase.
  - Check model: model loading errors, weight-loading latency, quantization mismatch errors.
- 60–120s: correlate traces and confirm root cause
  - Pull representative traces for affected request ids (trace sampling for tail requests).
  - Look for repeated span failures or long blocking spans (disk read, kernel scheduling, cuda memcpy).

Key metrics (definitions + recommended labels/aggregation):
- inference_requests_total
  - Definition: count of API requests accepted by our front proxy (post-auth).
  - Unit: requests
  - Aggregation: sum over 1m; group by route, region, customer_id, model_version
  - Use: blast radius, traffic shifts, sudden drops

- inference_responses_error_total
  - Definition: responses with 5xx or runtime-level error codes (including model fails).
  - Unit: errors
  - Aggregation: sum over 1m; group by error_code, route, model_version, region
  - Note: differentiate transport 5xx vs model-internal error codes (model->failure)

- inference_p90_latency_ms / inference_p99_latency_ms
  - Definition: client-observed end-to-end latency from request accept to final token emitted.
  - Unit: milliseconds
  - Aggregation: histogram buckets; use quantiles computed over 1m windows; group by route/model_version
  - Tagging: include sequence_length_bucket (short/medium/long) to avoid noisy baselines

- gpu_utilization_pct / gpu_memory_used_mb
  - Definition: per-GPU utilization and memory usage (exported from node exporter / DCGM).
  - Use: detect saturation / OOM patterns that cause preemption or queuing

- batch_queue_time_ms
  - Definition: time a request waits to be batched within the serving runtime before first token generation starts.
  - Unit: milliseconds
  - Aggregation: p50/p90/p99; tag by batching_policy, worker_pool, model_family
  - Why: sudden increase often explains latency spikes even when GPU util looks normal

- kv_cache_hit_rate
  - Definition: cache hits / (hits + misses) for prefix/KV caching layer.
  - Why: cache thundering or eviction storms reduce downstream compute efficiency

- model_load_time_ms
  - Definition: time from model pull request to model readiness signal.
  - Why: indicates slow storage or transient failures during deploys/rollouts

Tracing guidance (span names, attributes, sampling):
- Canonical span naming (keep short, stable):
  - span:proxy.request.accept
    - attrs: route, customer_id, request_id, region
  - span:runtime.enqueue
    - attrs: model_family, batching_policy, sequence_length, batch_size
  - span:runtime.kvcache.lookup
    - attrs: cache_hit(true/false), key_prefix_hash
  - span:runtime.model.forward
    - attrs: model_version, gpu_id, tokens_generated, input_tokens
  - span:runtime.io.read
    - attrs: src_type(s3/fs), bytes, latency_ms

- Sampling strategy:
  - Always sample 100% for error traces (inferred from status code or span tags).
  - Probabilistic sampling for normal traffic: 0.1% baseline, 2% for p99 latency requests, and 100% for requests chosen by alert rule.
  - Keep sampling decision in proxy and propagate via traceparent; avoid re-sampling at runtime layer.

- Useful attributes to add to every span:
  - customer_tier, route, model_version, region, gpu_id, node_id, batch_id, sequence_length_bucket

Dashboard layout (what to show in triage dashboard):
- Top row: blast radius and customer impact
  - total requests, affected routes list (top 10 by err rate), customer impact heatmap (customers by 5xx percent and revenue tier)
- Row 2: latency and error breakdowns
  - timeline p50/p90/p99 latency, errors by type, errors by component (proxy/runtime/model)
- Row 3: runtime health indicators
  - batch_queue_time p50/p90/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, worker_pool_queue_depth, inflight_batches
- Row 4: infra signals
  - GPU util/mem per node, pod restart rate, node-level cpu steal, disk IO wait for model pulls
- Drilldown panels (links from each widget):
  - From route -> route-level traces and top failing spans
  - From p99 latency spike -> distribution by sequence_length_bucket and batch_size
  - From GPU OOM -> pod logs and recent model loads on that node

PromQL examples (starter queries for playbook):
- total requests for route /chat over 1m:
  - sum(rate(inference_requests_total{route="/chat"}[1m]))
- p99 latency (histogram_quantile) over 5m by route:
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- batch queue p95 where many requests waiting:
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_queue_time_ms_bucket[1m])) by (le, worker_pool))
- kv cache eviction storm (miss rate rising):
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1m])) by (model_family) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_total[1m])) by (model_family)

Alerting heuristics (examples to codify later):
- P1: region-wide p99 latency > baseline + 400ms AND affected_customers > 5 -> page oncall
- P1: error rate > 5% of traffic for 5m for a high-revenue customer -> page and slack #customer-impact
- P2: sustained batch_queue_time p95 > 200ms for 10m -> notify paging list but only if correlated with gpu_util <80% (indicates batching misconfiguration)

Runbook steps (simple checklist for responder):
1) Identify affected routes/customers from triage dashboard.
2) Check cluster infra metrics for node-level OOM/restarts. If yes: pull node syslogs and escalate to infra.
3) If infra clean, inspect runtime metrics: batch_queue_time, kv_cache_hit_rate, worker_pool_queue_depth.
4) Fetch traces for a sample of failing/slow requests. Focus on top long spans and check span attributes.
5) If span shows runtime.io.read long -> check storage / s3 metrics and recent deploys.
6) If span shows runtime.model.forward long with high GPU memcpy -> check GPU memory fragmentation / driver errors.
7) Communicate mitigation: roll back model version, change batching_policy to smaller max_batch_size, or temporarily divert traffic to a fallback model.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add synthetic canaries that vary sequence_length to surface batching regressions earlier.
- Define exact baseline windows per route (weekday vs weekend baselines).
- Decide a conservative sampling budget for p99 traces to keep cost predictable.
- Build a small utility to map trace ids back to request ids and customer ids automatically in dashboards (linked to GitHub PR above).

Notes to self / ideas:
- Consider adding a compact "triage URL" template that pre-fills dashboard filters (region/route/customer) to speed handoffs.
- Prototype a histogram heatmap showing distribution of batch sizes vs latency for each model_family.

References and related docs:
- OBS-412: batch_queue_time metric refactor (Jira)
- inference-runtime PR #1892: trace propagation change
- Confluence: inference-observability canonical metrics page (linked above)

If you use this doc during a P1, please append short timeline notes at bottom (what checks you ran) so we can iterate on typical triage steps.

-- Maya
(questions / feedback ping #eng-observability on Slack)
